newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sees improved tourism revenue this year.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sees improved tourism revenue this year.

text.p: Croatia expects a handsome total revenue from tourism this year but the net profit for the country's flagship industry may be slim or none, local newspapers reported on Friday.
Daily Slobodna Dalmacija quoted Tourism Minister Niko Bulic as saying tourism revenue could be between 9.4 and 10.1 billion kuna ($2 billion) by the end of 1996.
However, since holidaymakers spent very little outside hotels, those earnings could almost entirely go for covering high operating costs and previous debts, he said.
To get the industry back on its feet, the government would have to help the industry reschedule its debt and get fresh, more favourable loans before the next season, he said.

Croatia has already borrowed abroad to rebuild those facilities which suffered most damage in the 1991 conflict with the separatist Serbs. That and a four-year war in neighbouring Bosnia scared away most tourists.

Seaside hoteliers accumulated huge losses from a much diminished trade during that period and tourism, once the main export industry and hard currency earner, was making only a fraction of its pre-war earnings.
They were estimated at $4 billion a year before Croatia broke away from former Yugoslavia.

But now that the peace has come to the troubled region, tourism is bracing itself for a full recovery. This summer already turned the tide of poor seasons as more foreign visitors returned to the Adriatic coast.
Bulic said the level of tourist revenue could quite fairly be gauged by some $1.2 billion in currency sold to local exchange offices in the first eigth months this year.
